entry.name: Clark v. Northeast Georgia Medical Center, Inc.
entry.synopsis: Plaintiff alleged that an unidentified hospital employee dropped her husband while transferring him from one bed to another, causing injuries that led to his death, and pleaded ordinary negligence without the expert affidavit required by OCGA 9-11-9.1. The trial court dismissed, finding that transferring a patient is an exercise of expert medical judgment. The Court of Appeals reversed, holding that, construing the complaint favorably to plaintiff, the alleged drop does not necessarily implicate a medical question and may instead be a physical act of strength and dexterity, and noting that the record did not establish that the unidentified employee was among the professionals covered by OCGA 9-11-9.1 (g).
entry.why: It clarifies that a patient fall during a physical transfer is not automatically a professional negligence claim requiring an expert affidavit, and that a defendant's status as a covered professional matters at the pleading stage.

additional_holdings.synopsis: The trial court also held that plaintiff could not cure the affidavit defect by an amended complaint filed after the two-year medical malpractice limitation period expired. The Court of Appeals reversed, holding that because the original complaint stated a claim for ordinary negligence, plaintiff was authorized under OCGA 9-11-15 (a) to amend as a matter of course to add an alternative professional negligence count with a supporting expert affidavit. Because the added claim arose from the same occurrence, it related back to the timely original complaint under OCGA 9-11-15 (c) and was not time barred.
additional_holdings.why: It confirms that an alternative professional negligence count with an expert affidavit, added after the limitation period, relates back to a timely complaint that stated an ordinary negligence claim arising from the same occurrence.
